subject.title: [Bug]: browser navigation-guard explicit hostname allowlist broken by SSRF loopback tightening (#100835)

question: Should browser navigation exact-host or pattern allowlist entries permit non-localhost hostnames that resolve to loopback, or should the trusted-host SSRF hardening retire that old test contract?
rationale: Both outcomes affect a security boundary: preserving the old contract restores an operator-declared browser exception, while retiring it keeps the accepted loopback DNS-rebinding hardening.

options.title: Retire the old loopback-alias contract
options.body: Keep the hardened trusted-host behavior and update browser navigation tests/docs to require explicit localhost, loopback literals, or broad private-network opt-in for loopback targets.

options.title: Approve a scoped browser exception
options.body: Allow the browser navigation guard to honor an explicit allowlist for the approved loopback case while continuing to block metadata and link-local DNS answers.

options.title: Defer to broader SSRF policy design
options.body: Keep this issue and the linked PR paused until exact-host trust and browser SSRF allowlists are decided together.

recommendation.title: Retire the old loopback-alias contract
recommendation.body: Keep the hardened trusted-host behavior and update browser navigation tests/docs to require explicit localhost, loopback literals, or broad private-network opt-in for loopback targets.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history across the linked SSRF hardening merge, adjacent browser/CDP policy work, and this security-boundary decision.
